steps.html:
Forty questions on Chapters 7, 8 and 9. No time limit, feedback as you go, and you can retake it as often as you like.

  • 40 questions · pass mark 70%
  • Grammar from Lessons 25–36
  • Vocabulary from all three wordlists
  • Function and register

steps.title: Lesson 25 · passive
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which is correct?
options: The device was invented by a group of students.
The device was invented from a group of students.
The device invented by a group of students.
steps.answer: The device was invented by a group of students.
steps.why: The agent takes by, and the passive needs the auxiliary.

steps.title: Lesson 25 · passive
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: When is the passive the better choice?
options: When the agent is unknown, obvious or unimportant.
steps.answer: When the agent is unknown, obvious or unimportant.
steps.why: Formality alone is not a reason; the question is whether the agent matters.

steps.title: Lesson 25 · passive
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'The prototype ___ tested at the moment.'
steps.answer: is being
steps.why: Present continuous passive: is/are being + past participle.

steps.title: Lesson 25 · vocabulary
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Suncayr is a marker you draw on your skin with, and the mark …
options: changes colour when the sun protection stops working
steps.answer: changes colour when the sun protection stops working
steps.why: That is what makes it an invention rather than a pen.

steps.title: Lesson 26 · purpose
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which expresses purpose?
options: The walls were removed, so conversation fell.
The walls were removed so that people would talk more.
The walls were removed because people talked more.
steps.answer: The walls were removed so that people would talk more.
steps.why: So that + a modal expresses intention; so alone states a result.

steps.title: Lesson 26 · purpose
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which is wrong?
options: They installed a gym in order to keep staff on site.
They installed a gym for to keep staff on site.
They installed a gym so as to keep staff on site.
steps.answer: They installed a gym for to keep staff on site.
steps.why: For to is not English; use in order to or so as to.

steps.title: Lesson 26 · reading
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: The argument behind workplace perks is that …
options: staff enjoy them and talk about them afterwards
anything that takes an employee out of the building costs the company time
they attract journalists and get the company written about
steps.answer: anything that takes an employee out of the building costs the company time
steps.why: The perks are an argument about time, not about generosity.

steps.title: Lesson 27 · vocabulary
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Putting something handmade into an industrial public space is mostly about …
options: protesting against decisions about public space
making an ugly public space more beautiful
advertising knitting the makers then sell
steps.answer: making an ugly public space more beautiful
steps.why: The contrast with the setting is the point, which is why it appears on lamp posts.

steps.title: Lesson 28 · softening
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which disagrees while leaving the other person room to retreat?
options: Isn't that a bit old-fashioned, though?
steps.answer: Isn't that a bit old-fashioned, though?
steps.why: A hedged question states a position and leaves the other speaker face.

steps.title: Lesson 28 · persuading
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'Wouldn't it ___ better to try the cheaper option first?'
steps.answer: be
steps.why: Wouldn't it be + adjective is the fixed frame for a soft proposal.

steps.title: Lesson 28 · vocabulary
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: A teacher described as strict but fair is one who …
options: applies rules only to some students
steps.answer: applies rules firmly and consistently
steps.why: Fair is what makes the strictness acceptable: it applies to everybody.

steps.title: Lesson 29 · punctuation and meaning
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which sentence says that all the engineers disagree?
options: The engineers who design these systems disagree.
The engineers, who design these systems, disagree.
Neither — the two mean the same.
steps.answer: The engineers, who design these systems, disagree.
steps.why: The commas make it non-defining: they all design the systems, and they all disagree.

steps.title: Lesson 29 · vocabulary
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: A fridge that orders milk when you run out is an example of …
steps.answer: the internet of things
steps.why: Everyday objects connected to a network.

steps.title: Lesson 30 · adjective collocation
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'She is very ___ about food.'
steps.answer: fussy
steps.why: Fussy about.

steps.title: Lesson 30 · adjective collocation
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which preposition follows suspicious?
steps.answer: of
steps.why: Suspicious of strangers.

steps.title: Lesson 30 · reading
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: The second text's central observation about generation labels is that …
options: labels are always wrong, whoever is using them
every generation gets the same words at the same stage of life
only researchers with the survey data can judge them
steps.answer: every generation gets the same words at the same stage of life
steps.why: The same adjectives recur every twenty years, applied to whoever is young.

steps.title: Lesson 30 · reading
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: The writer's final position on the labels is that they are …
options: worth abandoning, since they describe nobody accurately
useful for groups, useless for individuals
worth using more often, and about individuals as well
steps.answer: useful for groups, useless for individuals
steps.why: Used carefully they describe what a group lived through.

steps.title: Lesson 31 · adjective collocation
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'Quinoa is rich ___ protein.'
steps.answer: in
steps.why: Rich in.

steps.title: Lesson 31 · listening
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Ireland in the 1840s: what happened?
options: The potato crops failed and a million people died.
Potatoes arrived in the country for the first time.
Exports of grain to Britain doubled in a decade.
steps.answer: The potato crops failed and a million people died.
steps.why: The talk uses it as the cost of depending on a single crop.

steps.title: Lesson 32 · reviewing
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which softens a criticism so it does not sound like a rejection of the whole thing?
options: It was a waste of everybody's time and money.
The projection was the weakest part, but the rest worked well.
I didn't like a single thing about any of it.
steps.answer: The projection was the weakest part, but the rest worked well.
steps.why: Naming the part limits the criticism to that part.

steps.title: Lesson 32 · reviewing
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: 'It didn't live up to expectations.' This measures the thing against …
options: what the speaker had been led to expect beforehand
other things of the same kind
steps.answer: what the speaker had been led to expect beforehand
steps.why: Live up to always implies a standard set in advance.

steps.title: Lesson 33 · used to and would
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which is wrong?
options: We used to live by the sea.
We would live by the sea.
We would swim there every summer.
steps.answer: We would live by the sea.
steps.why: Would works for repeated actions but not for past states.

steps.title: Lesson 33 · used to and would
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'I ___ to the noise now.'
steps.answer: am used
steps.why: Be used to = accustomed; used to + infinitive = a past habit.

steps.title: Lesson 33 · reading
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Where does the detail in a very early 'memory' often come from?
options: from the event itself, stored intact
from dreams the person had later
steps.answer: from photographs and family retellings
steps.why: The memory is reconstructed from the account, then felt as first-hand.

steps.title: Lesson 34 · verb patterns
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'I look forward to ___ from you.'
steps.answer: hearing
steps.why: The to in look forward to is a preposition, so the -ing form follows.

steps.title: Lesson 34 · verb patterns
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which is correct?
options: I'm used to get up early.
I'm used to getting up early.
I'm used to got up early.
steps.answer: I'm used to getting up early.
steps.why: Same trap: be used to takes -ing.

steps.title: Lesson 34 · vocabulary
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Being bored because there is too little to do is best described as …
options: having nothing worth directing your attention at
working harder than the job actually requires
not getting enough sleep the night before
steps.answer: having nothing worth directing your attention at
steps.why: Three of the speakers describe under-work, not over-work.

steps.title: Lesson 35 · listening strategy
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: A speaker says 'come up with'. It means …
steps.answer: to think of and propose
steps.why: Come up with an idea or a solution.

steps.title: Lesson 35 · reading
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: The second text calls its own conclusion 'dull' because …
options: the research has not been published yet
it expects the advice to be rejected for being unexciting rather than wrong
the writer is not confident the finding is correct
steps.answer: it expects the advice to be rejected for being unexciting rather than wrong
steps.why: The whole text argues that the myth survives because it is satisfying.

steps.title: Lesson 36 · giving solutions
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which proposes rather than instructs?
options: What if we put up better lighting?
You need to put up better lighting.
steps.answer: What if we put up better lighting?
steps.why: What if opens a proposal for the other person to weigh.

steps.title: Lesson 36 · giving solutions
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'It might be worth ___ the wall first.'
steps.answer: checking
steps.why: Worth takes the -ing form.

steps.title: Lessons 25 and 26 · contrast
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which is a result, not a purpose?
options: The walls were removed so that people would talk more.
The walls were removed, so conversation dropped by seventy per cent.
The walls were removed in order to increase conversation.
steps.answer: The walls were removed, so conversation dropped by seventy per cent.
steps.why: A result reports what happened; a purpose reports what was intended.

steps.title: Lessons 33 and 34 · contrast
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which describes a state that has stopped?
options: I am used to living there.
steps.answer: I used to live there.
steps.why: Used to + infinitive, for a past state that is over.

steps.title: Lessons 28 and 32 · contrast
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which is the most hedged?
options: I'm not sure that's quite right.
steps.answer: I'm not sure that's quite right.
steps.why: Two hedges — not sure and quite — soften it furthest.

steps.title: Chapters 7–9 · vocabulary
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Something too large or important to be measured is …
steps.answer: immeasurable
steps.why: Immeasurable.

steps.title: Chapters 7–9 · vocabulary
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: To develop gradually over time is to …
steps.answer: evolve
steps.why: Evolve.

steps.title: Chapters 7–9 · vocabulary
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: A fixed idea about a group that is too simple to be fair is …
steps.answer: a stereotype
steps.why: A stereotype.

steps.title: Chapters 7–9 · vocabulary
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Not known to many people is …
steps.answer: obscure
steps.why: Obscure, and its opposite is renowned.

steps.title: Lesson 29 · vocabulary
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: A thermostat that learns your routine and adjusts itself is an example of a device that is …
steps.answer: connected
steps.why: Connected devices are what the internet of things is made of.

steps.title: Chapters 7–9 · function
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: You want to review something honestly without discouraging the maker. Which is best?
options: The idea is strong — the execution is what needs another pass.
I'd start again if I were you.
steps.answer: The idea is strong — the execution is what needs another pass.
steps.why: Separating idea from execution gives the criticism somewhere to land.

steps.title: Урок пройден
steps.sub: Block Test 3 · Lessons 25–36
items: I have tested the third quarter of the level.
I can use the passive, purpose clauses and verb patterns.
I can soften, propose and review.
I know the vocabulary of Chapters 7–9.
